items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist who will reply within 1 business day, but gives no immediate safety advice.

items.scenario: Customer says the email on their account was changed and two orders they don't recognise appeared.
items.flaw: Tells them to change their password and email back themselves, with no hand-off to a specialist.

items.scenario: Customer says they've opened a payment dispute with their bank because a refund for a returned throw is late.
items.flaw: Says the refund has been processed and asks them to withdraw the dispute, with no hand-off to a specialist.

items.scenario: Customer says their lawyer will be contacting the shop because a price adjustment was refused.
items.flaw: Re-explains the price adjustment policy, with no hand-off to a specialist.

items.scenario: Customer says their toaster filled the kitchen with smoke and set off the fire alarm.
items.flaw: Suggests cleaning the crumb tray, with no hand-off to a specialist and no advice to stop using it.

items.scenario: Customer's $1,200 rug shows as delivered but never arrived.
items.flaw: Suggests checking with neighbours and waiting two days, with no hand-off to a specialist.

items.scenario: Customer asks how long express shipping takes.

items.scenario: Customer asks how long they have to return an unused throw.
items.flaw: Hands the question to a specialist instead of answering it, though no escalation trigger applies.

items.scenario: A mug ($12) arrived cracked; the customer has a photo and wants a replacement.
items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist instead of arranging the replacement, though no escalation trigger applies.

items.scenario: Customer's order is 2 business days past its estimate and they're mildly annoyed.
items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist instead of handling it, though no escalation trigger applies.

items.scenario: Customer bought a lamp 4 days ago that's now cheaper and asks for the difference.
items.flaw: Hands the request to a specialist instead of handling the price adjustment, though no escalation trigger applies.

items.scenario: Customer placed an order 10 minutes ago and wants to cancel it.
items.flaw: Hands the request to a specialist instead of cancelling it, though no escalation trigger applies.

items.scenario: Customer's order worth $300 shows as delivered but never arrived.
items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist, though the order is under the $500 escalation threshold, instead of handling it.

items.scenario: Customer asks once, politely, whether a manager could look at their refund question.
items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist immediately, though a manager has only been asked for once, instead of answering the refund question.

items.scenario: Customer sees a charge on their card for an order they didn't make on their account.
items.flaw: Tells them to contact their bank, with no hand-off to a specialist.

items.scenario: Customer got an alert that someone logged in to their account from another country and changed the address.
items.flaw: Hands the case to a specialist but says they will reply within 5 business days instead of 1.

items.scenario: Customer asks how long they have to return an unused lamp.
items.flaw: Condescending: says the 30 days is 'clearly stated' on every page and implies they didn't bother to look.

items.scenario: Customer's standard order placed 4 business days ago hasn't arrived; they ask where it is.
items.flaw: Blames the customer for not reading the delivery estimate in their order confirmation.

items.scenario: Customer's order is 6 business days late and they're frustrated.
items.flaw: Sarcastic about the delay ('shocking, I know').

items.scenario: Customer writes a detailed, polite message about a cracked bowl ($14) delivered yesterday, with a photo.
items.flaw: Curt to the point of dismissive: one line, no greeting or empathy.

items.scenario: Customer asks a second time when their refund will arrive; the return reached the warehouse 2 days ago.
items.flaw: Passive-aggressive: opens with 'per my last email'.

items.scenario: Customer asks whether they can return a clearance cushion they changed their mind about.
items.flaw: Shouts that clearance is FINAL SALE in capital letters, twice.

items.scenario: Customer's message has several spelling mistakes; they ask about express shipping times.
items.flaw: Mocks the customer's spelling.

items.scenario: Customer's order is 2 business days late; they politely ask for an update.
items.flaw: Lectures the customer about being patient.

items.scenario: Customer reports a chipped vase delivered 9 days ago, with a photo.
items.flaw: Scolds them for not reporting it sooner, although they're within the 14 days.

items.scenario: Customer asks how to start a return for unused towels.
items.flaw: Overly familiar slang: opens with 'hey dude' and treats it like a chat with a friend.

items.scenario: Customer politely complains that their refund is taking a while; the return arrived 4 days ago.

items.scenario: Customer's $80 order shows as delivered but they say it never arrived.

items.scenario: Customer bought a toaster for $59 five days ago, now $54, and asks for the difference.
items.flaw: Rude about the small amount ('fine, here's your $5').

items.scenario: Customer asks where to find the tracking link for their order.
items.flaw: Condescending about technology ('tracking links really aren't that hard').

items.scenario: Customer asks again when their refund will arrive; the return reached the warehouse yesterday.
items.flaw: Impatient: opens with 'Again?' and a sigh.

items.scenario: Customer placed an order 3 hours ago and wants to cancel it.
items.flaw: Sarcastic about the customer's change of mind.

items.scenario: Customer has complained twice about late deliveries and asks about their latest order, 1 business day late.

items.scenario: Customer is disappointed that a clearance vase can't be returned.
items.flaw: Blames the customer for choosing a clearance item.

items.scenario: Customer asks how the price adjustment policy works.
items.flaw: Talks down to them: 'let me explain this very slowly'.

items.scenario: Customer asks a detailed question about returning a lamp they changed their mind about.

items.scenario: Customer asks how long express shipping takes.
items.flaw: Uses capital letters and several exclamation marks for the delivery times.

items.scenario: Customer placed an order 2 hours ago with the wrong address and asks to change it.

items.scenario: Customer dropped their kettle and asks whether the warranty covers the cracked lid.
items.flaw: Condescending: says most people know warranties don't cover drops.

items.scenario: Customer asks a follow-up question about how long the refund for their returned rug takes.
items.flaw: Ends with 'please don't email again about this'.

items.scenario: Customer asks for a price adjustment on cushions bought 6 days ago that are now cheaper.
items.flaw: Accuses the customer of trying to get free stuff, while granting the adjustment.

items.scenario: Customer asks how long they have to report a damaged item.
items.flaw: Writes the whole reply in capital letters.

items.scenario: Customer wants to return an unused patterned throw because they don't like it after all.
items.flaw: Mocks the customer's taste in choosing it.

items.scenario: Customer politely asks whether their order placed 2 days ago has shipped.
items.flaw: Tells the customer to calm down, although they're polite.

items.scenario: Customer's order placed before a public holiday is 1 business day late; they ask for an update.
items.flaw: Snarky about the customer expecting deliveries over the holiday.

items.flaw: Belittles the question ('even a child can print a label').
